Jamie (Support): Hey team — customer hitting intermittent 503s on /v1/generate. They gave a trace hash a3b9f4e7b102f6d9c8a. Can someone pull server-side logs for that trace and confirm if it was a model OOM, gateway timeout, or something else? Also: what KQL should I run and what's the retention?

Maria (SRE): Can you paste the exact full trace id and the approximate customer timestamp/account? The snippet looks truncated.

Jamie (Support): Full trace: a3b9f4e7b102f6d9c8a. Customer reported at 2026-03-16T22:14:03Z, account corp-acme-123.

Maria (SRE): Thanks — for quick checks use this KQL in Kibana (hot cluster):
```
index: "redwood-prod-logs-*"
trace.id: "a3b9f4e7b102f6d9c8a"
| sort @timestamp desc
```
Hot logs: 30 days retention. Cold/archive: up to 365 days but different index pattern (redwood-archive-*); queries there take longer and may require the ops team.

Alex (ProdEng): If the customer can repro, have them include the trace header to preserve the client side trace:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "X-Trace-Id: a3b9f4e7b102f6d9c8a" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-rlhf","input":"<trimmed>"}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Also ask them to add `X-Debug: true` header so we can correlate additional debug fields.

Ben (Infra): If nothing shows in hot, query the archive via ES directly (may need SRE/infra to run):
```
POST /redwood-archive-*/_search
{
  "query": { "term": { "trace.id": "a3b9f4e7b102f6d9c8a" } },
  "size": 100
}
```
If you need, I can run it and attach the raw hits.

logs-bot: starting search on redwood-prod-logs-2026.03.16 for trace a3b9f4e7b102f6d9c8a :mag_right:

Maria (SRE): I pulled hot logs and found the request. Relevant sanitized snippets: 
```
[2026-03-16T22:14:03Z] trace=a3b9f4e7b102f6d9c8a gateway: upstream response 502 from model-worker-12; worker stderr: "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory"
[2026-03-16T22:14:03Z] trace=a3b9f4e7b102f6d9c8a autoscaler: attempt=1 -> scheduled retry; fallback routed to gateway, returned 503 to client
```
Looks like model worker OOM that bubbled up and the gateway translated to 503.

Maria (SRE): Next steps: 1) Ask customer to run the curl above with X-Trace-Id & X-Debug: true so we get a richer debug payload. 2) I will generate an internal debug bundle for that trace (note: debug bundles are retained for 7 days). If we need older raw logs beyond 30 days hot retention, we will have to pull from archive (up to 365 days) — that takes ops coordination.

Jamie (Support): Got it. I'll send the curl + header instructions to the customer and request the debug bundle. Please attach the snippet you found to the ticket. Thanks! :thumbsup:

Ben (Infra): FYI I queued an archival search on redwood-archive-* just in case; results will be linked here when done.

Jamie (Support): Perfect — I'll update the customer with repro steps and ask for the debug bundle. Will follow up once they send it. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
